engine_bytes.rule: The board pins the engine inputs by sha256 (evaluation_engine_inputs and the files named by the engine command). The placeholders resolve to an export of spellbench bb20077 for the adapter files, the pinned python.exe, the pinned catalog and the pinned bridge. Before `bench commit`, run `spellbench bench prepare benchmarks/pauper-ladder-v3 --check` from a clean checkout of the default branch, with the pinned python.exe and with every placeholder resolved from benchmarks/local.json: it must print OK. The check prepares the definition again and compares the bytes, so the engine identity, the nine bot identities and the 18 matchups are the committed ones; it refuses any placeholder of the definition that is also set in the process environment (usually MTG_KERNEL_V2_BRIDGE and MTG_KERNEL_PUBLIC_CATALOG; remove MTG_KERNEL_V2_SOURCE too), and the builtin bot identities hash the interpreter and the checkout's builtin bot sources. Drive `bench commit` and `bench run` the same way. A commitment cannot be redone.
engine_bytes.prepare_check: `bench prepare --check` on this definition, 2026-11-15, in a scratch copy with the pinned python.exe and the bridge, catalog and source variables removed from the process: OK (the committed bytes are the prepared bytes). With the bridge and catalog variables set it refused; under another interpreter it reported the two builtin bot identities as different. Rerun it from a clean checkout of the default branch before `bench commit`.
engine_bytes.against_pauper-ladder-v2_2.1.0: Only kernel_history_v2.py and kernel_observation_v2.py differ from that board's engine files (spellbench d4dcb42). The bridge, the scorer, the catalog, python.exe and the other adapter files are byte for byte the same, and all nine bot identities are equal to that board's. This board's engine command is kernel_engine_v2.py, so kernel_engine_infoset_v2.py and kernel_g6_digest.py are not engine inputs here.

board.games: 15 rung matchups (7 rungs, band 3) plus 3 entrant matchups of chains-a-c4-u1048576 (Basilisk 2) against g115, oh2-r2s1-b512 and oh2-r2s1-b512-argmax: 18 blocks of 64 seat-swapped pairs, one pair per ordered pairing of the eight decks, 128 games a block, 2,304 games
board.deferred: oh2-r2s1-b512-s4a-16k-k4 is in deferred_entrants: it stays in the roster, bench prepare schedules none of its blocks, and the board lists it as pending until its own entrant-only run. Its placement on pauper-ladder-v2 is a record of that board and not a rating here.
board.validity: Enforced by code (unit spellbench-validity/v1 in benchmark.json, docs/design/2026-11-15-validity-unit.md). Every denominator is the scheduled count. Per block: at least 125 of 128 games natural and at least 63 of 64 pairs complete. Per bot: at least 97% of its scheduled games natural. Per ordered deck pairing over the run: at least 33 of 36 games natural (90%, one game always allowed). Forfeits of any cause, halts, truncations and games not played count against natural. `bench run` writes the verdict and the tables into the manifest. A failing run is published in full and revealed, is not rated, shows no rating, is excluded by its own record, and is never topped up or replaced: bench prepare does not schedule its matchups again under this evaluation. `bench compose` applies the unit again to the blocks it combines.
board.number: A rating is Elo against the reference bots over every ordered pairing of the eight decks. Unequal decks pull scores toward even, so the scale is this board's own: no v3 number is compared with a pauper-ladder-v2 or pauper-grid-v1 number. Per-deck ratings are not published (deck_slices false).

infoset_off.ruling: Evaluation 3.0.0 runs without x_kernel_infoset_v1. The exporter halts with engine_fault:infoset:I1 when a token is returned to its owner's hand and a decision is posed before it ceases to exist (Snap on an opposing token; mtg-kernel#713). None of the 252 mirror games of the sweep reached it. No scheduled bot reads the export. A bot that needs it (the search entrant) joins later through a per-block opt-in under a new evaluation version, with the exporter fixed first. Evaluation 3.0.0 does not offer per-block extensions and does not forbid them: the extensions are a field of the definition and of the snapshot contract, and a later evaluation version defines the opt-in.

play_is_unchanged.what: The same scheduled games (same config, run secret, game secrets and bot seeds) played with the extension and without it, the engine traffic recorded by a line tap. Sample 1: the sweep run above with the extension, its 18 halted games and 25 natural Faeries off-mirror games. Sample 2: this board's 18 blocks under a fresh secret, 3 off-mirror pairs in each block: 108 games, 54 ordered deck pairings, every deck on the play and on the draw, every scheduled bot.
play_is_unchanged.natural_games_result: every ledger field equal except game_digest, which chains the engine traffic and so names the enabled extensions; the traffic is identical message for message once the extension's own payload and name are removed, with the one field the information-set path adds to the x_kernel_flat_v4 payload (known_hand_masked_observation_sha256, read only by the search bot) and the request ids (counters, which the game digest leaves out too)
play_is_unchanged.halted_games_result: each matches the game without the extension message for message up to the request the halt answered, and ends naturally without it

v4_visibility.what_it_tests: At every decision of neutral private-support games on the eight board decks, the acting seat's V4 boundary and x_kernel_flat_v4 encoding are unchanged when the search sampler redeterminizes every hidden card the engine's knowledge tables mark as unknown to that seat; and every place one player learned hidden cards of the other (library look or reveal, hand reveal, library reorder revealed to the opponent) is a reviewed site marked in the source. It is a consistency check against the engine's own knowledge tables plus a pinned enumeration of reveal sites, not a proof against a fact the tables wrongly mark as known.
v4_visibility.same_sites_as_89fb69a95: the same 14 calls at the same lines as the 4fccd3ebc receipt (the repair is in push_paid_activation, after the last reveal site); same 16 games, 4,731 decisions, 14,193 sampled worlds
v4_visibility.coverage: The audit exercised 6 of the 25 marked library-reveal calls and 8 of the 36 marked hand-reveal calls. The 21 and 35 present at 89fb69a95 rest on the static enumeration reviewed in mtg-kernel #462 and #476; the 4 library and 1 hand marked calls added since are premodern card code from mtg-kernel #465 and #467, outside this board's pool. No library reorder call is marked as revealing to the opponent.
